changes.records: Fixed destination records separate recovery separators from active reservations. Admission is atomic; observer callbacks follow reservation. Nonthrowing scope-bound completion releases every admitted record, including streamed emergency failure paths. Completion and source ownership are explicit; prompt failures do not make external events.
changes.prompt: Snapshots and admission both gate presentation. Deferral is not delivery failure, does not set sticky failure status, and retains input for a later flush. Null-buffer binding initializes explicitly. Return from injected to native retains existing fresh-row behavior.
changes.inspection: Monotonic per-observation tickets prevent older cache publication; one same-attempt reinspection refreshes an overtaken observation. Cache/epoch eligibility cannot silently suppress byte delivery. Continuing fd replacement keeps borrowed-descriptor best-effort semantics.
changes.fallback: Replaced standard-stream metadata uses guarded snapshots and epoch/serial commits, without mutable shared references across unlocked I/O. Actual injected I/O and buffer replacement remain caller-synchronized.
changes.guards: Single-bit, nonzero and pairwise uniqueness checks supplement bank/capacity guards. Scope-bound stderr capture and cout buffer restoration cover test assertion/exception exits.

Check formatting, Python, shell and workflows

performance.method: Identical Release flags and seven byte-identical harness/support files. One warm-up plus five measured samples per variant/workload, two sets. Three-build order rotates and reverses across samples. No concurrent tests or analyzers.
performance.allocation_and_work_checks: Positive controls verify 1000 allocations/32000 bytes, 1000 geometry queries, and 128 write/stat/flags/bounds operations. Empty warning polls and unchanged redraws allocate/prepare/write zero bytes. Append preparation remains bounded and allocations match the baseline.
performance.lock_instrumentation: Separate objects count NativeMetadataGuard acquisitions, with 1000-reset positive controls for all three variants. Instrumented timings are excluded.
performance.gate: Candidate reduced locks and improved editing, but diagnostic benefits did not repeat consistently; large regular-file export medians regressed 1.41% and 0.33%. Omit the candidate. These observations are not claims of causal timing differences; there are no timing-based CI thresholds.
performance.pilot: Initial pilot samples are published separately and excluded from acceptance. Final measurement sets copy and hash identical support sources across every variant.

limitations: Native metadata synchronization does not serialize complete diagnostic byte streams; concurrent bytes may interleave.
Injected-stream I/O and rdbuf replacement remain caller-synchronized. Concurrent interactive cli_main invocations are not introduced.
Concurrent descriptor replacement retains borrowed-descriptor best-effort destination semantics; no atomic fd binding is promised.
Emergency and standalone delivery remains best effort without EAGAIN waiting, with eight total EINTR retries. Partial duplicates and conservative extra separators remain allowed.
Blocking TTY output remains outside the bounded-cancellation guarantee.
Native PPC/Tiger compiler, SDK and runtime are unavailable. The host cross-selection build verifies interposer exclusion and link/runtime behavior, not native Tiger execution.
